title: Adopt minimum GitHub integration controls for single-maintainer V0.1

spec.unmetRequirement: Consequential changes require explicit accountable human approval, deterministic proof and a separate integration decision. The observed main branch has no effective integration rules. The earlier proposal additionally assumed a second human reviewer, but req-authority and pol-engineering require accountable human judgment, not a two-person organization. A single-maintainer model must realize the enforceable integration obligations without pretending that GitHub approval counts establish the owner's judgment.
spec.simplestViableOption: Use one active branch ruleset for main to require PR-based integration and the existing check, and protect branch history and deletion. Keep explicit owner approval of consequential transitions and the later decision to integrate as separate attributable process obligations using existing decision and Git/PR evidence conventions. Defer independent peer review. Add no collaborator, bypass, synthetic approval, approval bot, service or agent authority.
spec.selectedOption: Create one ruleset named Golden Path main with target=branch, enforcement=active, conditions.ref_name.include=[refs/heads/main], conditions.ref_name.exclude=[] and bypass_actors=[]. Its pull_request rule has required_approving_review_count=0, dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push=false, require_code_owner_review=false, require_last_push_approval=false and required_review_thread_resolution=false. Preserve merge, squash and rebase methods. Its required_status_checks rule requires context=validate with integration_id=15368 (GitHub Actions), strict_required_status_checks_policy=false and do_not_enforce_on_create=false. Add non_fast_forward and deletion rules, with no others. This zero is the absence of an independent GitHub review-count requirement, not the absence of accountable-owner approval. Before consequential implementation, the owner must explicitly approve the identified transition and scope; the agent may faithfully record that actual statement, source, date and scope in the existing decision approval fields, but never supply or approve it itself. After implementation and checks, the owner inspects the actual diff and evidence and separately decides whether to integrate the identified PR/head revision. Scope changes require renewed owner consideration; no GitHub stale-review mechanism enforces this process in the selected model. Reverify check identity and current rules before authorized application. All paths receive the same mechanical gate; the owner reviews changes to the gate itself.
spec.capabilityGained: PR/check/history preconditions implemented through GitHub, with owner approval and integration decisions separately attributable and reviewable. The owner has explicitly authorized only the named ruleset and safe non-merging probes. cap-github-governance records that task-scoped administrative execution boundary; no merge, general administration, deployment or reusable external-write adapter is added. Configuration and enforcement outcomes require separate evidence.
alternatives: Keep successful CI and documented review expectations without protection: insufficient because integration is not blocked when the requirements are unmet.
Equivalent legacy branch protection: acceptable if it enforces the same behavior, including administrators; prefer one ruleset rather than maintaining overlapping sources of platform configuration.

Require one independent GitHub approving review: deferred, not a current V0.1 invariant. One is the smallest nonzero count, but that does not earn the requirement for another person. GitHub authors cannot approve their own PRs; only krnese is currently an eligible collaborator. An owner-authored PR would be blocked by organizational structure that this workload has not earned. Do not add a nominal reviewer or change PR authorship merely to satisfy the control.

Add CODEOWNERS or path-specific peer review: deferred until legitimate additional owners, distinct expertise, risk or an operating model earns mandatory independent review. A same-owner mapping does not solve owner-authored PR approval.

Require the branch to be up to date: deferred. The existing contract requires checks against an identified revision and base, not serialized integration against the latest target. Earlier passing checks do not prove compatibility with later target changes.

Enable stale-review dismissal or latest-push approval now: deferred together with mandatory peer review. Stale dismissal cannot make an absent qualifying review bind the owner's separate process approval; latest-push approval would reintroduce a different-person requirement. Changed scope and final revision still require accountable-owner decisions, but their authenticity and freshness are not enforced by this ruleset.

Configure standing emergency bypass: deferred because no exception has been authorized. An empty bypass list is the initial absence of a grant, not a universal prohibition on break-glass behavior. A future exception must identify trigger, actor, scope, evidence, restoration and retrospective review.
Install bots, merge queues, custom policy services, scheduled monitoring or new agent capabilities: not earned by this baseline.
spec.simplerOptionAssessment: req-authority distinguishes proposed and approved state; pol-engineering names explicit human task approval and review; adr-bootstrap-minimum records approval by the human owner without requiring a second human. The contract therefore supports the single-maintainer model. Required independent PR approval was an implementation assumption, not an approved engineering requirement. Removing that assumption is an explicit proposal, not a workaround to make a probe pass. The preserved observations remain historically correct; missing PR/check/history controls still matter even though peer-review absence is no longer proposed as a failure criterion. Native rules authorize accounts, not human-versus-agent intent. An agent with the owner's authenticated CLI or browser may technically merge a green PR or alter rules; repository instructions and approval fields cannot mechanically prevent that. The proposed model must retain this limitation rather than claim enforced separation. Force-push and deletion restrictions earn their place through req-learning; default-branch deletion and automatic cleanup of merged topic branches are distinct.
spec.operationalResponsibility: krnese remains the accountable owner. The explicit approval below authorizes implementation, not integration of repository changes. Re-read the live identity, permissions, target, rules and check publisher before applying the exact settings; stop on drift or missing authority. Preserve 90-day retention, read-only workflow defaults, disabled Actions PR approval, disabled auto-merge and current merge methods. Do not add collaborators, bypass actors or other rulesets. Preserve API results and partial failures; after an ambiguous write read back before retrying, never create duplicate rulesets blindly. Do not automatically remove protection as rollback. Any correction outside the approved settings needs a new owner decision. The safe probe may create synthetic commits on an isolated topic branch and a clearly marked non-merging PR, observe failing then passing CI, and close that probe without merging. It must not publish the local governance diff. Isolated-target destructive rejection tests require an equivalent separately authorized target; do not create a second ruleset or test destructive operations on live main to obtain that proof. An agent must not supply owner approval or infer integration permission from credentials, passing checks or GitHub eligibility. Owner-performed integration remains outside this capability. Shared owner credentials remain an unenforced separation risk.
spec.rationale: On 2026-09-24 the user challenged the independent-review assumption and clarified that explicit accountable human approval does not require a second human. The requirements, policy, approved bootstrap decision and single-collaborator observation support that distinction. The earlier one-review and stale-dismissal settings were never applied. The owner subsequently explicitly approved implementation of the minimum PR/check/history/deletion ruleset with zero required reviews and no bypass, while withholding integration permission. Approval status records that human decision, not configuration success, peer review or enforcement proof. Preserve both earlier failed observations unchanged. Future independent review may be earned by real role-separation, production/security consequence, compliance, expertise or evidence of owner-only review failure; team size alone does not select a quorum. Authentication, structural checks, portability and hook trials cannot substitute for owner decisions or platform evidence.

approval.statement: I explicitly approve implementation of that scoped governance change. Implementation is approved. Integration is not.
approval.scope: Adopt the selected minimum ruleset on krnese/golden-path main: PR-based integration, verified validate GitHub Actions check, force-push and deletion protection, no bypass actors, zero required GitHub approving reviews, existing merge methods, and all other controls deferred. Re-read live state, apply only that ruleset, verify configuration, run only the previously defined safe non-merging probes, preserve evidence and validate repository changes. No merge or integration of repository changes, destructive test against live main, collaborator grant, broader governance, portable-entry-point work or hook experiment.
